newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday February 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday February 19.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Returning from a visit to Germany, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said that a corrective mini-budget later this year was "very probable", but the government would have to wait a few more weeks before deciding if it was absolutely necessary (all).
* Hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti said he was totally opposed to an extra budget for 1997 adding it would be a "serious error" (all).

* The lira tumbled to 997.5 to the mark amid concerns that Italy might not make it in the first wave of EMU. Belgian central bank chief Alfonse Verplaetse apparently questioned the lira's ability to join EMU early, although he later denied he had been referring to Italy (all).
* Mondadori shares fell 10 percent after the shock resignation of managing director Paolo Forlin (all).
* Italy's December producer prices rose 0.5 percent year-on-year, but fell 0.1 percent on a monthly basis, the lowest level in the last 10 years (all).
* A report by state economic research institute ISCO said Italy is likely to end 1997 with economic growth of 1.3 percent against 0.8 percent estimated for 1996 (all).

* Car maker Fiat Auto confirmed that it is to hire an extra 2,000 workers on fixed-term contract in its Italian plants, due to rising car orders reflecting a national car buying incentive scheme (all).
* Investment bank IMI SpA said it would boost its stake in Italy's largest bank Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino to 5 percent from 2 percent previously (all).

* Prime Minister Prodi said German financiers and industrialists were interested in investing in state telecommunications holding group STET once it has been privatised. Prodi was in particular referring to German company Siemens which already owns 50 percent of telecommunications firm Italtel (La Repubblica, Il Sole 24 Ore).
* European Commissioner Karel Van Miert is reportedly considering to launch an enquiry over the 1994 privatisation of food company Cirio-Bertolli-De Rica (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* Banca Commerciale Italiana is said to be in "advanced negotiations" to buy Credito Bergamasco from France's Credit Lyonnais in an operation worth 800 billion lire (La Stampa).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
